source_text:
Contra Severum Antiochenum (fragmentum ap. Pseudo-Anastasium
Sinaitam, Contra monophysitas)
89.1189 Ὀλυμπιοδώρου τοῦ μεγάλου φιλοσόφου διακόνου Ἀλεξανδρείας, ἐκ τοῦ
δευτέρου λόγου τοῦ κατὰ Σεβήρου, ἐν ᾧ παραγαγὼν τὴν χρῆσιν τοῦ ἁγίου
Ἀθανασίου τὴν λέγουσαν τὰ δύο θελήματα ἐπὶ Χριστοῦ, οὕτω πως διεξέρχεται
λέγων·
thought_title: Lemma introducing Olympiodorus's quotation of Athanasius on two wills
orientation: A later compiler introduces a fragment from Olympiodorus's second book against Severus, reporting that he quoted Athanasius on the two wills in Christ and then expounded it.
pass_a_gloss: Of Olympiodorus the great philosopher, deacon of Alexandria, from the second book of the work against Severus, in which, having brought forward the quotation of Saint Athanasius that says the two wills in Christ, he goes through it in some such way, saying:

choices.why: Glossary requires 'book' for λόγος in the sense of a division of a multi-part work; 'discourse' and 'treatise' are banned.
Glossary requires 'quotation' for χρῆσις as a cited passage from an authority; 'use', 'citation', and 'testimony' are banned.
Glossary requires 'wills' for θελήματα in the Christological sense of the two wills in Christ; 'acts of will', 'desires', 'intentions', and 'volitions' are banned.
The aorist participle of παράγω means to introduce or bring forward a quotation; 'having adduced' is also possible but 'brought forward' matches the lemma's framing of citing an authority.
The verb means to expound or go through in detail; 'expounds' is the natural English for the lemma's report, but 'goes through' preserves the literal sense of the Greek compound.
